lessons.subject: English literature
lessons.title: An Inspector Calls
lessons.summary: Explore how Priestley uses the Birling family to argue for social responsibility.
lessons.curriculum: GCSE English literature: British fiction or drama from 1914 onwards
pages: JB Priestley wrote ‘An Inspector Calls’ in 1945, but set it in 1912. The audience knows about the world wars that the characters cannot foresee.
Inspector Goole questions the wealthy Birling family about the death of a young woman, Eva Smith. Each of them played a part in her death.
Mr Birling believes “a man has to mind his own business and look after himself”. The Inspector argues the opposite: “We are members of one body. We are responsible for each other.”
The younger characters, Sheila and Eric, accept their guilt and change. Their parents mostly do not, which shows Priestley's hope for the young.

check.question: When is ‘An Inspector Calls’ set?
check.explanation: Priestley set the play in 1912, before the First World War.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Trigonometry in right-angled triangles
lessons.summary: Use sine, cosine and tangent to find sides and angles.
lessons.curriculum: GCSE maths: the trigonometric ratios sin θ, cos θ and tan θ, and using them to find angles and lengths in right-angled triangles
pages: In a right-angled triangle, name the sides from the angle θ: the opposite side, the adjacent side and the hypotenuse.
sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse and tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent. Many people remember this as SOH CAH TOA.
If the hypotenuse is 10 centimetres (cm) and θ = 30°, the opposite side = 10 × sin 30° = 10 × 0.5 = 5cm.

check.question: Which ratio is opposite ÷ adjacent?
check.explanation: tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent: the TOA in SOH CAH TOA.

lessons.subject: Chemistry
lessons.title: The periodic table
lessons.summary: Find out how the periodic table groups elements that behave alike.
lessons.curriculum: GCSE combined science, chemistry: the periodic table, and groups 0, 1 and 7
pages: The periodic table lists the elements in order of atomic number. Columns are called groups, and rows are called periods.
In 1869, Dmitri Mendeleev left gaps in his table for elements nobody had discovered yet. Later discoveries filled them.
Elements in the same group have the same number of electrons in their outer shell, so they react in similar ways.
Group 1, the alkali metals, react with water and get more reactive down the group. Group 0, the noble gases, have full outer shells, so they are very unreactive.

check.question: Why are the noble gases so unreactive?
check.explanation: With full outer shells, noble gas atoms do not need to gain or lose electrons.

lessons.subject: Physics
lessons.title: Current, potential difference and resistance
lessons.summary: Use V = I × R to work out values in a circuit.
lessons.curriculum: GCSE combined science, physics: potential difference = current × resistance (V = IR)
pages: Current is the flow of electric charge. It is measured in amps (A).
Potential difference, often called voltage, is measured in volts (V). Resistance makes it harder for current to flow, and is measured in ohms (Ω).
Potential difference = current × resistance, or V = I × R.
If I = 2A and R = 6Ω, then V = 2 × 6 = 12V.

check.question: A current of 4A flows through a 3Ω resistor. What is the potential difference across it?
